title: Draft SME policy aims for 25 lakh new jobs by 2031
excerpt: The Prime Minister said the National SME Policy 2026 will go to the cabinet soon. It targets 35% of GDP from small firms and easier loans for women and young entrepreneurs.

image.alt: A fruit seller in his small shop in Dhaka
image.credit: File photo: Masumcity / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
The government aims to create 2.5 million (25 lakh) new jobs through small and medium enterprises by 2031 under a draft National SME Policy 2026, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said on Sunday (22 November), The Daily Star reported. The draft will go to the cabinet for approval soon.

The policy targets a 35% share of GDP from SMEs by 2031. It promises easier loans, training and incentives for women and young entrepreneurs, links to banks and foreign buyers, and a National Creative and Design Centre to improve product design and packaging. It also pushes small firms to move beyond garments into leather goods, light engineering, agro-processing, plastics, handicrafts and IT. The article does not give the current SME share of GDP.

The Prime Minister was opening the 13th National SME Product Fair, organised by the SME Foundation under the Ministry of Industries, at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre. It runs until 28 November. Of the 380 enterprises taking part, about 60% are owned by women. The SME Foundation plans to train at least 50,000 entrepreneurs over five years.

Why it matters

Many NGO livelihood and microfinance programmes support small and micro businesses. Credit is the main barrier, especially for women. With private credit growth weak, the targets will depend on whether banks actually lend to small borrowers.

What to watch

The cabinet's approval and the final text, especially any targets for women-led firms and for SME lending.

Sources
